audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Lillia or Skill at levels 3, 4-5 and first item while the prose underneath said the opposite — whys[2] 'he owns this overstep window', whys[3] 'a full E-W Sett out-trades you', whys[5] 'lets him facetank your DoT'. The packet chart also reads Sett on all three rows.
audit.why: A reader saw 'Lillia 7/10' at Levels 4-5 next to a sentence explaining that Sett wins Levels 4-5. Also diff read HARD while tone, diffRating 4/10 and breakdown.difficulty all read favoured.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 proposed as matched full+content pairs (Lillia at 1; Sett at 3, 4-5 and first item), ratings adjusted, whys rewritten, diff aligned to FAV with the other four fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sett's spike was described only as 'bruiser first item'; the page never connected it to Grit.
audit.why: Haymaker spends stored Grit for both a shield and its damage, so his item spike and his survivability against your DoT are the same mechanic.
audit.corrected: First-item stage now names Grit as the reason he walks through the burn, and the 2+ item row keeps Lillia because Facebreaker's 10s cooldown is the only catch tool he has.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real interactions were absent and one asserted fact was false. Facebreaker only stuns if it catches enemies on opposite sides of him — a lone target is slowed instead. Haymaker deals true damage in the centre and physical on the sides. Your own damage is what stores as his Grit. And the page twice described an 'out-of-mana Sett' — every Sett ability costs 0.
audit.why: The one-side slow rule changes where you stand in every trade; the centre/side split changes whether his W is a chunk or a kill; and 'your poke feeds his Haymaker' inverts how you use the DoT while he is holding W.
audit.corrected: All three stated, the mana claim removed and replaced with the Facebreaker cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10), and The Show Stopper restated as a 400-range grab on 120/100/80 rather than an instant point-and-click.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole content layer was written in the first person ('I sit at max range', 'my squishy body') against the site's second-person voice.
audit.why: Every other matchup addresses the reader directly; this one reads like someone else's diary.
audit.corrected: early, mid, late, all four spikes and the wants lines converted to second person inside the length band.

edits.after: Facebreaker lands at 3, and one grab into a Grit-loaded Haymaker takes a third of your health bar.

edits.after: Track Facebreaker: it only stuns if it catches enemies on both sides of him — stand alone, away from his minions, and it is a slow instead of a pin.

edits.after: Sett has only his double-punch and no Grit stored yet, so farm with the Q sweetspot from range and concede nothing he can punish.

edits.after: Once your W and Dream Dust tick real max-health damage and Q move speed stacks, a Sett whose 10s Facebreaker is down can never catch you — burn him from range.

edits.before: Level 1 is actually mine — Sett only has his passive double-punch and no stored W yet, so I sit at max range and farm with the Q sweetspot, conceding nothing. The trouble starts at 2 and especially 3: once he has E he can grab-stun my squishy body out of nowhere, and a stunned Lillia with no defensive button eats his stored W true-damage smash for a brutal chunk. Never throw a Q from inside E range, never get shoved to the wall, and keep my Dream Dust DoT ticking from outside his grab so he pays HP just for walking at me.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Sett has no Grit stored and only his double-punch, so sit at max range and farm the Q sweetspot, conceding nothing. Trouble starts at 3, when Facebreaker comes up on a 16s cooldown: it stuns only if it catches enemies on opposite sides of him, so alone and away from his minions you are slowed instead — that difference decides whether the Haymaker lands. Never Q from inside its 490 range, never get shoved to the wall, and keep Dream Dust ticking from outside the grab so he pays HP to walk at you.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are his strongest window and I have to respect it. With full E-W online he wins any trade where he lands the grab — E pins me, the stored true-damage W smash lands center, and the double-punch finishes before my Q hops carry me out. I keep my distance, stack Q move speed, and chip with E Swirlseed slows and Dream Dust rather than dueling. At 6 it's a coin flip: my Lilting Lullaby sleep can blunt his all-in if I land it, but his R suppress is an instant point-and-click that ignores my kite entirely, so don't sleep-bait into a Sett who still has ult up.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are his strongest window. With Facebreaker and Haymaker online he wins any trade where the grab lands — E pins you, the Grit-loaded W puts true damage dead centre, and the double-punch finishes before your Q hops carry you out. Stand off-centre, stack Q move speed, and chip with Swirlseed slows rather than dueling. Every point of damage you land is stored as his Grit, so poking a Sett who is holding W only loads the gun. At 6 it is a coin flip: Lullaby blunts his all-in, but The Show Stopper is a 400-range grab — never sleep-bait a Sett with ult up.

edits.before: This is where I claw it back. Once my Liandry's/Blackfire and W are online, the Dream Dust DoT and W slam tick for real percent-HP, and my passive plus Q move-speed stacks make me genuinely uncatchable for an out-of-mana Sett whose E is on cooldown. The plan is simple: survive his lane bully phase without feeding kills, then convert the 2-item window into roams and skirmishes where I burn him from range and never stand in grab distance. If he's even or ahead, though, his grit and E-W-R all-in still delete me the second he catches me — so I want this to be a kite war on my terms, not a brawl.
edits.after: This is where you claw it back. With Liandry's online, Dream Dust and the W slam tick real max-health damage, and your passive plus Q move-speed stacks make you uncatchable for a Sett whose Facebreaker is on its 10s cooldown. The plan is simple: survive his bully phase without feeding, then convert the two-item window into roams and skirmishes where you burn him from 700 range and never stand inside grab distance. If he is even or ahead, his Grit and the E-W-R chain still delete you the moment he catches you — keep it a kite war, never a brawl.

notes: Two data problems worth the user's attention. (1) The packet reports winRate 33.33 on only 9 games while the brief header reports 1279 games for this matchup — those cannot both describe the same sample, and every difficulty field on the page is built as if Lillia is favoured. I aligned diff to the other four fields rather than to the 9-game win rate. (2) The content layer for this matchup is the only one I have seen written in the first person; that is a template-level defect and other Sett pages may share it.
